Articles like this piss me off because they fail to disclose pertinent information. First, when comparing the dollar figure, are they adjusting for inflation? Writers (and fans) like to paint a movie as being the "biggest" but rarely do they ever actually discuss tickets sold. How can anyone claim this is the biggest R-rated movie opening ever without disclosing how many people paid to see it? Tickets cost between $15-$20 in most urban markets these days. Back in the 70s they cost $2.50. Before hyping up a film as the greatest thing ever, it would seem salient to discuss how many tickets were actually sold.

And even that doesn't tell the whole story....the US population is about triple the size it was in 1970 so to get a true gauge of of a film's cultural appeal you'd have to take into account the percentage of the population that bought a ticket as well if you really wanted to compare apples to apples.

The reason this shit annoys me so much is that I have read these type of reports over and over and over again throughout the years. They seem intended to just hype whatever cool movie is in vogue. The stats they throw around are almost always hollow and without context. Deadpool has gotten great reviews, and it seems to be doing well at the box-office. But to claim it is the biggest R-rated film of all time seems ludicrous to me, and I suspect if I cared enough to do a little research, such a claim would be easily refuted.

Is bronchitis contagious? Does anybody knows?

Anything with "-itis" means "inflammation of". Bronchitis is inflammation of the bronchial tubes (airways of the lungs).

So anything with an "-itis" is a symptom and symptoms in and of themselves are not contagious.

Whatever is causing the symptom is what's possibly contagious.

If you have bronchitis from smoking, then it's not likely contagious as the cause is years and years of damage from chronic smoke exposure. If you have it from some kind of cold or flu, then yes, it's definitely probably contagious.
